### Sour Grapes
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/sour-grapes-one-year-devotions-for-men-december-6.html
Passage: Ezekiel 18:2
Points:
- When facing suffering, people naturally look for someone else to blame.
- Israel's exiles quoted a proverb blaming their ancestors rather than facing their own sin.
- God rejected this proverb and affirmed that each person answers for their own wrongdoing.
- Upbringing and environment influence us, but they do not eliminate personal moral accountability.
- Accepting individual responsibility is necessary to receive God's personal grace and forgiveness.

### The Devil's Favorite Proverb
Author: Dr. Jeff Schreve
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/fromhisheart/from-his-heart-week-of-october-28-2016.html
Passage: Ezekiel 18:2-3
Points:
- The proverb of sour grapes reflected deceptive thinking that excused Israel's guilt.
- Shifting blame onto previous generations leads people to accuse God of being unfair.
- Believing judgment is someone else's fault causes fatalism and removes motivation to do right.
- God's ways are just, and He holds every person accountable for their own choices.
- Rather than excusing sin, believers are called to repent and live in daily faith.
